active_paradigms.idea: Dense interface hotspot cluster: use 5 tightly-clustered contact residues B77/B80/B82/B83/B84 to saturate the core binding epitope
active_paradigms.description: The contact list shows B77, B80, B81, B82, B83, B84 form a dense spatial cluster on IL-7Ralpha. Using 5 of these (B77, B80, B82, B83, B84) instead of 3 sparse hotspots provides much denser epitope coverage. This forces the binder to engage the entire hydrophobic/charged patch rather than isolated anchors. Keep B84 as the proven anchor, add B82/B83 (adjacent residues with strong contacts), B80 (nearby contact), and B77 (tightest contact at 2.73A). Drop B143 which is distant from this cluster. Increase binder length slightly to [70, 110] to accommodate engagement with the larger epitope surface. Use seed=42 for fresh exploration. Keep sc_scale_score at 1.5 (slightly reduced from 1.8 to avoid over-constraining the dense epitope). Use tan noise for local_latents which is smoother than 1/t2 and may better handle the complex multi-residue interface.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: best_total_reward via denser epitope engagement, diversity_bonus via more constrained but varied designs
active_paradigms.cautions: 5 hotspots is more constraining - ensure binder_length is sufficient to reach all hotspots. B81 is also a candidate but 5 is a good balance. Verify all residues are in ALLOWED_HOTSPOTS.

active_paradigms.idea: Maximize diversity bonus with beam-search algorithm and broader length range to generate more unique sequence types
active_paradigms.description: The evaluator's combined_score includes a diversity_bonus of up to 0.10 based on unique aatype sequences. Switching from best-of-n to beam-search with n_branch=2 and beam_width=2 explores more of the design space and can produce more diverse sequences. Use a wider binder length range [60, 120] with num_length_samples=2 to sample different length classes. Keep the proven hotspots B77, B84, B143 but use seed=99 for fresh exploration. Reduce sc_scale_score to 1.2 for both channels to allow more sequence diversity rather than forcing convergence to a single interface mode. Use power schedule (p=1.5) for bb_ca to spread backbone denoising, and uniform schedule for local_latents to maximize sequence diversity. This approach targets the diversity_bonus component which can add up to 0.10 to the score.
active_paradigms.cautions: beam-search with n_branch=2 beam_width=2 is capped to 2 in stage2. Wider length range increases sampling diversity. Ensure beam_search params are within GPU memory limits.

active_paradigms.idea: Optimize sampling parameters: use 1/t noise for both channels with higher p values and stronger sc_scale_score=2.0 with reduced noise scale for sharper interface definition
active_paradigms.description: The current program uses 1/t2 for local_latents which is very sharp near t=0 but may cause instability. Switch both noise modes to the stable 1/t with p=1.5 for bb_ca and p=2.0 for local_latents to get controlled sharpness. Increase sc_scale_score to 2.0 (maximum effective range before diminishing returns) for both channels to maximize self-conditioning guidance. Reduce sc_scale_noise to 0.05 (near-zero) to minimize noise injection during self-conditioning, making the conditioning signal cleaner. Use hotspots B77, B82, B84, B143 (4 hotspots: tightest contact + adjacent + hydrophobic core + C-terminal anchor) for better spatial coverage than 3 hotspots. Use log schedule p=2.0 for bb_ca (concentrate early backbone steps) and power p=3.0 for local_latents (concentrate side-chain refinement very close to t=0). Seed=7 (evaluator default) which may have been well-tuned for this target.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: best_total_reward via sharper self-conditioning and cleaner noise schedule
active_paradigms.cautions: sc_scale_score=2.0 is aggressive - monitor for mode collapse. 1/t noise with p>1 effectively scales the noise; ensure p values stay in 0.05-8.0 range. Four hotspots provides good coverage without over-constraining.
